intent.raw_query: Istanbul cultural exploration, $1800 solo, historical sites and cuisine, May 2026

experiences.name: Hagia Sophia & Blue Mosque Exploration
experiences.description: Spend a morning exploring the iconic Hagia Sophia, a UNESCO World Heritage Site that has served as a cathedral, mosque, and museum over its 1,500-year history. Then walk to the nearby Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) to admire its stunning six minarets and intricate Iznik tile interior. Hire a local guide for deeper historical context.

experiences.name: Grand Bazaar & Spice Bazaar Food & Shopping Tour
experiences.description: Wander through the Grand Bazaar, one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Then head to the nearby Egyptian Spice Bazaar to sample and purchase Turkish spices, dried fruits, lokum (Turkish delight), and saffron. Engage with local vendors and taste free samples of authentic flavors.

experiences.name: Traditional Turkish Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class led by a local chef in a traditional Istanbul kitchen. Learn to prepare classic dishes such as meze platters, stuffed grape leaves (dolma), lamb kebabs, and baklava. Includes a visit to a local market to source fresh ingredients, followed by a communal meal with fellow travelers.

experiences.name: Topkapi Palace & Harem Tour
experiences.description: Explore the magnificent Topkapi Palace, the administrative and residential center of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Walk through the Imperial Harem, the Treasury housing the Topkapi Dagger and Spoonmaker's Diamond, and the sacred relics pavilion. The palace offers breathtaking views of the Bosphorus and Golden Horn.

experiences.name: Bosphorus Sunset Cruise with Street Food Evening
experiences.description: Board a traditional wooden boat for a scenic Bosphorus cruise at sunset, passing by Ottoman-era yalı mansions, the Rumeli Fortress, and the iconic suspension bridges connecting Europe and Asia. After docking, explore the Karaköy waterfront for a street food evening featuring simit (sesame bread rings), balık ekmek (fish sandwiches), and fresh pomegranate juice.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Istanbul
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Istanbul Airport at 13:00. Take the budget-friendly Havaist airport bus (approx. 50 TRY) to the city center. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront area. Freshen up and get oriented with a leisurely walk along the nearby waterfront promenade to shake off travel fatigue.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the nearest local neighborhood market or bazaar street. Pick up a simple street-food dinner and get your first taste of Istanbul's vibrant evening atmosphere. Explore the immediate surroundings of the hotel.

meals.breakfast: On the plane or skip
meals.lunch: Grab a quick simit (sesame bread ring) and tea from a street vendor near the airport or bus stop — under 30 TRY
meals.dinner: Local street food near the hotel: try a döner wrap or balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from a street stall — approx. 60–80 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some currency at the airport or use an ATM for Turkish Lira. Avoid hotel currency exchange due to poor rates. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Get to bed early to prepare for a full Day 2.

day_by_day.morning: Start with an early visit to the iconic Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya). Arrive before 9:00 AM to beat crowds. Entry is free as it is now an active mosque — dress modestly and bring a scarf. Spend 1.5–2 hours marveling at the Byzantine mosaics, massive dome, and layered history spanning nearly 1,500 years.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 5 minutes to the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii) — free entry, also requires modest dress. Afterward, explore the Hippodrome Square and its ancient monuments: the Obelisk of Theodosius, the Serpent Column, and the German Fountain. Then head to the nearby Arasta Bazaar for budget souvenir browsing.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the atmospheric streets of Sultanahmet at dusk. Enjoy tea at a traditional çay bahçesi (tea garden) overlooking the Sea of Marmara. End the evening with a peaceful sit in the park between Hagia Sophia and the Blue Mosque, which is beautifully lit at night.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a local bakery: fresh börek (cheese or spinach pastry) and çay — approx. 40–60 TRY
meals.lunch: Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi — one of Istanbul's oldest and most beloved budget eateries. Köfte (meatball) plate with bread and ayran — approx. 120–150 TRY
meals.dinner: Lezzet-i Şark or a similar local lokanta (Turkish canteen-style restaurant) near Sultanahmet. Choose a daily set menu (tabldot) — approx. 100–130 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — Sultanahmet involves a lot of cobblestone walking. The area is very tourist-heavy; be cautious of carpet shop touts and 'friendly strangers' offering unsolicited tours.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapi Palace (Topkapı Sarayı), the grand residence of Ottoman sultans for nearly 400 years. Budget entry is around 500–600 TRY; the Harem section costs extra (~300 TRY) but is highly recommended. Spend the morning exploring the Imperial Treasury, the sacred relics, and the stunning views over the Bosphorus from the palace terraces.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk downhill to the Gülhane Park — one of Istanbul's oldest and largest public parks, free to enter. Enjoy a peaceful afternoon stroll among rose gardens and shaded paths. Then visit the Istanbul Archaeology Museums complex nearby (approx. 200 TRY entry) — three museums in one showcasing ancient artifacts from across the Ottoman Empire's vast territories.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Eminönü waterfront. Watch the bustle of ferries and fishermen on the Galata Bridge. Enjoy the lively evening atmosphere around the Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) area.

meals.breakfast: Simit, white cheese, olives, and çay from a local kahvaltı (breakfast) spot near the hotel — approx. 60–80 TRY
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from a local market or grab a lahmacun (Turkish flatbread pizza) and ayran from a street stall near Gülhane — approx. 60–80 TRY
meals.dinner: Balık ekmek (grilled fish sandwich) from the iconic floating boats at Eminönü dock — approx. 80–100 TRY. Add a cup of boza or fresh juice from nearby stalls.

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace is closed on Tuesdays — visiting today (Monday) is perfect. Arrive early to avoid long queues. The Archaeology Museum is an underrated gem that most tourists skip.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. It's free to enter and opens at 9:00 AM. Browse lanes of spices, textiles, ceramics, jewelry, and leather goods. Practice your bargaining skills — initial prices are often 2–3x the fair value.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk 10 minutes to the Spice Bazaar (Egyptian Bazaar / Mısır Çarşısı) — free entry. Sample Turkish delight, dried fruits, nuts, and spices. Buy affordable edible souvenirs here. Then walk across the Galata Bridge to the Karaköy neighborhood for a change of scenery and explore its hip, artsy streets.
day_by_day.evening: Climb up to the Galata Tower (Galata Kulesi) for panoramic views of Istanbul at sunset — entry approx. 200–250 TRY. Afterward, explore the lively streets of Beyoğlu and İstiklal Avenue, Istanbul's famous pedestrian boulevard lined with historic buildings, street musicians, and local shops.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Turkish breakfast spread at a local kahvaltı salonu in Sultanahmet — eggs, cheese, olives, tomatoes, bread, çay — approx. 80–120 TRY
meals.lunch: Eat at a lokanta inside or near the Grand Bazaar. Try mercimek çorbası (lentil soup) and bread — approx. 80–100 TRY
meals.dinner: Beyoğlu side street restaurant: pide (Turkish flatbread with toppings) or a full kebab plate at a local spot off İstiklal Avenue — approx. 120–160 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Pickpocketing can occur in crowded bazaars — keep bags in front and valuables secure. İstiklal Avenue is best explored on foot; the historic red tram is mostly for photos now.

day_by_day.morning: Take a budget Bosphorus ferry from Eminönü or Karaköy to Üsküdar on the Asian side (approx. 25–35 TRY with an İstanbulkart transit card). Visit the Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi) — an iconic small tower on a tiny island in the Bosphorus. View it from the Üsküdar waterfront (visiting inside costs extra). Explore Üsküdar's charming local streets and traditional mosques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a short dolmuş (shared minibus) or walk to Çamlıca Hill (Büyük Çamlıca) — Istanbul's highest point with sweeping 360-degree views of the city, Bosphorus, and Princes' Islands. Entry to the hill and its park is free. Enjoy the stunning panorama and the peaceful gardens.
day_by_day.evening: Return by ferry to the European side. Spend the evening at the Karaköy or Cihangir neighborhood — both have a relaxed, bohemian vibe. Browse independent bookshops, vintage stores, and local cafés.

meals.breakfast: Grab a classic Turkish breakfast from a street cart: simit, boiled egg, and çay — approx. 40–60 TRY
meals.lunch: Eat like a local in Üsküdar at a neighborhood lokanta. Try kuzu tandır (slow-roasted lamb) or etli pilav (rice with meat) — approx. 100–130 TRY
meals.dinner: Karaköy or Cihangir: try a meze spread at a meyhane (Turkish tavern) — share small plates of hummus, cacık, stuffed grape leaves, and grilled halloumi — approx. 150–200 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Get an İstanbulkart rechargeable transit card (25 TRY card fee + load credit) if you haven't already — it gives discounted fares on all public transport including ferries, buses, and trams. The Asian side feels noticeably less touristy and more authentic.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Süleymaniye Mosque — arguably Istanbul's most magnificent mosque, built by the legendary architect Mimar Sinan in 1557. It's free to enter and far less crowded than the Blue Mosque. The mosque complex includes a medrese, hamam, and the tombs of Suleiman the Magnificent and his wife Hürrem Sultan. Spend time in the tranquil courtyard gardens with sweeping city views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding Süleymaniye neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most authentic and least touristy old districts. Walk through the historic streets of Vefa (try the famous Vefa Bozacısı shop for boza, a traditional fermented drink). Then head to the Fatih district to explore its traditional market streets and the Fatih Mosque.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Eminönü and take a relaxing evening walk along the Golden Horn waterfront promenade. Visit the Miniaturk park area if interested (small fee), or simply enjoy the illuminated bridges and waterfront cafés.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local fırın (bakery): fresh bread, cheese, olives — approx. 50–70 TRY
meals.lunch: Eat at the famous Tarihi Süleymaniye Işkembecisi or a nearby lokanta for a hearty soup and bread lunch — approx. 80–100 TRY
meals.dinner: Fatih neighborhood: try a traditional Turkish home-cooking restaurant. Order mantı (Turkish dumplings with yogurt and paprika butter) — approx. 100–130 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The Süleymaniye area is a wonderful place to observe everyday Istanbul life away from the tourist crowds. Bring a scarf for mosque visits. The Vefa Bozacısı shop is a historic institution — definitely try the boza (served cold with roasted chickpeas on top).

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — a group of car-free islands in the Sea of Marmara, a 1–2 hour ferry ride from Kabataş terminal (approx. 60–80 TRY each way with İstanbulkart). Head to Büyükada, the largest island. Rent a bicycle (approx. 100–150 TRY/day) and explore the island's Victorian-era mansions, Greek Orthodox Monastery of St. George at the hilltop, and pine forests.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue cycling or take a horse-drawn carriage (phaeton) tour of the island. Relax on one of the small beaches or swim in the clear Sea of Marmara (weather permitting in May). Enjoy the car-free, peaceful atmosphere — a world away from Istanbul's chaos.
day_by_day.evening: Take the evening ferry back to Istanbul. The sunset views of the Istanbul skyline from the returning ferry are absolutely spectacular. Arrive back at Kabataş and take the tram back toward your hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before departure — simit and çay from Kabataş ferry terminal — approx. 40–50 TRY
meals.lunch: Fresh fish lunch at one of the island's waterfront restaurants — grilled sea bass or sea bream with salad and bread — approx. 150–200 TRY (splurge-worthy for the setting)
meals.dinner: Simple and quick dinner near the hotel after the ferry return — a pide or lahmacun from a local fırın — approx. 80–100 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Friday ferries can be crowded — book or arrive early. The Princes' Islands are a UNESCO World Heritage Site candidate. No motorized vehicles are allowed on the islands (except emergency services). Bring sunscreen and water for the cycling/hiking.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii) — a stunning Byzantine church turned mosque famous for its extraordinarily well-preserved 14th-century mosaics and frescoes. Located in the Edirnekapı neighborhood near the ancient city walls. Entry fee approx. 200–250 TRY. Spend the morning appreciating some of the finest surviving Byzantine art in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along a section of the Theodosian Walls — the ancient land walls built in the 5th century AD that protected Constantinople for over 1,000 years. Explore the Edirnekapı gate area and the Blachernae Palace ruins nearby. Then head to the Balat and Fener neighborhoods — Istanbul's most colorful and historically rich districts with Greek Orthodox, Jewish, and Armenian heritage.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Balat's famous rainbow-colored houses and antique shops. The neighborhood has become an artsy enclave with independent cafés and galleries. Enjoy a sunset coffee at a rooftop café overlooking the Golden Horn.

meals.breakfast: Balat neighborhood kahvaltı: a full traditional Turkish breakfast spread at one of the charming local cafés — approx. 100–130 TRY
meals.lunch: Grab a quick sandwich or börek from a local bakery in Edirnekapı — approx. 60–80 TRY
meals.dinner: Balat or Fener: try a local meyhane for affordable fish and meze. Look for fixed-price set menus — approx. 150–180 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Balat is one of Istanbul's most photogenic neighborhoods — bring your camera. The area has been gentrifying but still retains its authentic neighborhood character. Wear good walking shoes as the streets are steep and cobblestoned.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Istanbul Modern Art Museum (İstanbul Modern) in Karaköy — entry approx. 250–300 TRY. It houses an excellent collection of modern and contemporary Turkish art and photography. The building itself offers great Bosphorus views. Spend 2 hours exploring the galleries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk up to the Tophane neighborhood and explore the historic Tophane-i Amire (Ottoman cannon foundry). Then head to Cihangir — a bohemian hillside neighborhood beloved by artists and expats. Browse its antique shops, bookstores, and quirky cafés. Walk down to Karaköy's waterfront for the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Turkish hamam (bathhouse). The Çemberlitaş Hamamı (built 1584) or Kilic Ali Pasa Hamamı offer authentic experiences. Budget options start around 400–600 TRY including scrub and soap massage. A quintessential Istanbul cultural experience.

meals.breakfast: Karaköy's famous Karaköy Güllüoğlu pastry shop: fresh baklava and börek for breakfast — approx. 80–100 TRY
meals.lunch: Cihangir neighborhood: a simple Turkish home-cooking café — daily soup, main course, and bread — approx. 100–120 TRY
meals.dinner: Post-hamam dinner: you'll be relaxed and hungry. Try a hearty kuzu şiş (lamb skewer) or Adana kebab at a local ocakbaşı (grill restaurant) — approx. 150–180 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Book the hamam in advance if possible, especially for weekend evenings. Most hamams have separate sections or times for men and women. The hamam experience is one of the most culturally immersive things you can do in Istanbul.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Beşiktaş neighborhood — a lively, working-class district with a famous open-air market (especially vibrant on weekday mornings). Visit the Çırağan Palace (exterior only — it's now a luxury hotel, but the Ottoman facade along the Bosphorus is stunning and free to admire). Walk along the Bosphorus promenade from Beşiktaş toward Ortaköy.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach Ortaköy — a picturesque waterfront neighborhood famous for its baroque-style mosque right on the Bosphorus and its weekend market. Try the famous Ortaköy kumpir (giant stuffed baked potato with various toppings) — a must-eat Istanbul street food. Browse the craft stalls along the waterfront.
day_by_day.evening: Continue walking or take a bus to Bebek — one of Istanbul's most affluent and scenic Bosphorus-side neighborhoods. Enjoy an evening stroll along the Bebek waterfront. Watch the boats on the Bosphorus as the sun sets. Take a bus back toward the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Beşiktaş market: fresh simit, fruit, white cheese, and olives from market stalls — approx. 50–70 TRY
meals.lunch: Ortaköy kumpir (stuffed baked potato) with multiple toppings — a filling and famous street food — approx. 80–120 TRY
meals.dinner: Beşiktaş neighborhood lokanta: a simple but delicious set menu dinner — approx. 100–130 TRY

day_by_day.notes: The walk from Beşiktaş to Ortaköy along the Bosphorus is one of Istanbul's most scenic urban walks. Ortaköy is particularly lively on weekends but also pleasant on weekday afternoons. Bebek's café scene is pricier — stick to walking and enjoying the atmosphere for free.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dolmabahçe Palace — the opulent 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus shore. Guided tours are mandatory and cost approx. 400–500 TRY. The palace contains 285 rooms, 44 halls, 68 toilets, and the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier. It's a jaw-dropping display of Ottoman-European fusion architecture.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a bus to the Yıldız Park and Yıldız Palace area — a large forested park with walking trails, pavilions, and great Bosphorus views. The park is free to enter. Visit the Yıldız Hamidiye Mosque (free entry). Enjoy a peaceful afternoon among the trees — a rare green escape within the city.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Nişantaşı neighborhood — Istanbul's upscale shopping and dining district. Window-shop along the elegant streets and people-watch at outdoor cafés. Find an affordable side-street restaurant for dinner before returning to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the hotel — approx. 60–80 TRY
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic for Yıldız Park: buy fresh bread, cheese, tomatoes, and fruit from a nearby market — approx. 60–80 TRY total
meals.dinner: Nişantaşı side street: look for a pide salonu or a simple Turkish restaurant off the main shopping streets — approx. 120–150 TRY

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays — visiting on Tuesday is perfect. Photography inside the palace is restricted. The palace tour can take 2–3 hours. Yıldız Park is a hidden gem that most tourists miss entirely.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Bosphorus public ferry cruise — not a tourist cruise, but the regular commuter ferry from Eminönü/Beşiktaş that runs up the Bosphorus to Anadolu Kavağı (the last stop at the mouth of the Black Sea). Round trip costs approx. 60–80 TRY with İstanbulkart — an incredible budget alternative to expensive tourist boats. The 90-minute journey passes under the Bosphorus bridges and alongside historic yalıs (waterfront mansions).
day_by_day.afternoon: At Anadolu Kavağı, climb up to the ruined Genoese castle (Yoros Kalesi) for panoramic views where the Bosphorus meets the Black Sea — free to visit. Explore the small fishing village. Take the return ferry back to the city in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your second-to-last evening in the Kapalıçarşı/Sultanahmet area doing any last-minute souvenir shopping or revisiting favorite spots. Enjoy a rooftop dinner with views of the illuminated Hagia Sophia and Blue Mosque.

meals.breakfast: Early departure breakfast: simit and çay from the Eminönü ferry terminal — approx. 40–50 TRY
meals.lunch: Fresh fish lunch at Anadolu Kavağı — the village is famous for its fish restaurants. Grilled fish, salad, and bread — approx. 150–200 TRY (worth the splurge for fresh Bosphorus fish)
meals.dinner: Sultanahmet area rooftop restaurant: a set menu with Bosphorus views — approx. 200–250 TRY (a special last-night-before-last splurge)

day_by_day.notes: The public Bosphorus ferry (IDO/Şehir Hatları) is one of Istanbul's best-kept budget secrets — the same scenic journey as expensive tourist boats at a fraction of the cost. Check the ferry schedule in advance as departures are limited. Anadolu Kavağı is a charming, sleepy village worth the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul. Visit any missed sights or return to a favorite spot. Consider the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — a magnificent underground Byzantine cistern beneath Sultanahmet with atmospheric lighting and ancient columns — entry approx. 300–350 TRY. Or simply take a final peaceful walk along the Bosphorus waterfront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for checkout. Pack up and do a final check of belongings. Head to the airport via Havaist bus or metro. Allow plenty of time for Istanbul traffic, especially in the afternoon. Do last-minute Turkish delight or spice purchases at the airport duty-free if you forgot any gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure. Reflect on 13 incredible days exploring one of the world's greatest cities — from Byzantine mosaics to Ottoman palaces, from Bosphorus ferries to street-food feasts.

meals.breakfast: Final Turkish breakfast at a beloved local spot near the hotel — make it count! — approx. 100–130 TRY
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel before checkout: a gözleme (stuffed savory crepe) or börek from a street stall — approx. 60–80 TRY
meals.dinner: Airport or on the plane

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3–3.5 hours to get to Istanbul Airport from the city center, accounting for traffic. The Havaist bus is the most budget-friendly airport transfer option. Keep some Turkish Lira for last-minute purchases, tips, and transport. The Basilica Cistern is undergoing renovations periodically — check ahead for current access.

trip_options.title: Classic Istanbul Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Istanbul Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront district. Check-in, freshen up, and settle into your room.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront promenade near the hotel to get your bearings. Explore the immediate neighborhood, visit a local çay (tea) garden, and soak in your first views of Istanbul's coastal scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Head to a nearby waterfront restaurant for your first taste of Turkish cuisine. Explore the local harbor area, watch the sunset over the water, and enjoy a relaxed first evening.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (mid-flight)
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a casual lokanta (Turkish canteen) near the hotel upon arrival — try mercimek çorbası (lentil soup) and fresh bread.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a mid-range waterfront meyhane (tavern) near the hotel — order mezze platters, grilled balık (fish), and ayran.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 activities begin only after 13:00 arrival. Keep the evening light to recover from travel. Exchange some currency to Turkish Lira at the airport or a local exchange office.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the iconic Hagia Sophia (Ayasofya) — one of the world's greatest architectural achievements. Arrive early to beat the crowds. Explore the stunning Byzantine mosaics, Ottoman calligraphy medallions, and the massive dome interior.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Sultanahmet Square and visit the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Camii). Admire its six minarets and exquisite İznik tile interior. Then explore the ancient Hippodrome of Constantinople and its monuments — the Obelisk of Theodosius and the Serpent Column.
day_by_day.evening: Wander through the Sultanahmet district as the historic buildings are illuminated at night. Enjoy a traditional Turkish dinner in the area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local simit (sesame bread ring) with cheese and tea from a street vendor.
meals.lunch: Köfteci Ramiz or a similar mid-range lokanta in Sultanahmet — try köfte (meatballs) with pilaf and salad.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tarihi Sultanahmet Köftecisi or a comparable traditional restaurant — lamb dishes, pide bread, and baklava for dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Hagia Sophia requires modest dress (shoulders and knees covered). The Blue Mosque is closed to tourists during prayer times — plan around the schedule. Wear comfortable walking shoes.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Topkapi Palace (Topkapı Sarayı) — the magnificent seat of the Ottoman Empire for nearly 400 years. Explore the Imperial Treasury, the Harem quarters, and the sacred relics in the Pavilion of the Holy Mantle.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the adjacent Gülhane Park — Istanbul's oldest public park — for a peaceful afternoon stroll. Then visit the Istanbul Archaeological Museums (Arkeoloji Müzeleri) nearby, housing artifacts from across the ancient world including the Alexander Sarcophagus.
day_by_day.evening: Take a short ferry ride across the Golden Horn to the Karaköy district. Explore the vibrant waterfront and enjoy dinner in this trendy neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a traditional Turkish breakfast spread at a local kahvaltı salonu — cheeses, olives, eggs, tomatoes, honey.
meals.lunch: Café or snack kiosk inside Topkapi Palace grounds — gözleme (stuffed flatbread) or a light sandwich.
meals.dinner: Mid-range restaurant in Karaköy — try fresh seafood meze and grilled octopus with a glass of rakı.

day_by_day.notes: Topkapi Palace and the Harem require separate tickets. Book online in advance to avoid long queues. The palace is closed on Tuesdays.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Grand Bazaar (Kapalıçarşı) — one of the world's oldest and largest covered markets with over 4,000 shops. Browse carpets, ceramics, spices, jewelry, and textiles. Practice your bargaining skills!
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk to the nearby Spice Bazaar (Mısır Çarşısı) in Eminönü and sample Turkish spices, lokum (Turkish delight), dried fruits, and nuts. Then stroll along the Galata Bridge, watching fishermen and enjoying views of the Golden Horn.
day_by_day.evening: Climb the Galata Tower (Galata Kulesi) for panoramic 360-degree views of Istanbul at sunset. Explore the charming Galata neighborhood with its cobblestone streets and bohemian cafés.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a börek (flaky pastry) with tea from a local pastane (pastry shop).
meals.lunch: Street food lunch near the Spice Bazaar — balık ekmek (fish sandwich) from a boat vendor at Eminönü, with a glass of şalgam (turnip juice).
meals.dinner: Dinner in the Galata/Beyoğlu area — try a mid-range meyhane with live Turkish folk music.

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays. Beware of pickpockets in crowded market areas. The Galata Tower has an elevator but expect queues — book tickets online.

day_by_day.morning: Cross to the Asian side of Istanbul via ferry from Eminönü to Kadıköy. Explore the vibrant Kadıköy market (Kadıköy Çarşısı) — a foodie paradise with fresh produce, specialty shops, and street food stalls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Wander through Moda neighborhood — a charming, upscale residential area with seaside parks, vintage shops, and independent cafés. Visit the Moda Coastline for beautiful Bosphorus views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the European side by ferry — enjoy the magical twilight crossing. Have dinner in the Beşiktaş or Ortaköy neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a simit with tea.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Kadıköy market — çiğ köfte (spiced bulgur rolls), kokoreç (offal sandwich), or fresh mussels stuffed with rice (midye dolma) from street vendors.
meals.dinner: Dinner near Ortaköy — try kumpir (loaded baked potato) as a famous local street food, followed by a sit-down dinner at a mid-range Bosphorus-view restaurant.

day_by_day.notes: The ferry ride itself is a highlight — sit on the upper deck for the best views. Kadıköy is very walkable. Keep some cash handy as some market vendors don't accept cards.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Basilica Cistern (Yerebatan Sarnıcı) — a stunning underground Byzantine cistern with atmospheric lighting, ancient columns, and the famous Medusa head bases. Then explore the nearby Çemberlitaş (Column of Constantine).
day_by_day.afternoon: Discover the Süleymaniye Mosque — Sinan's masterpiece and one of Istanbul's most beautiful Ottoman mosques. Explore the surrounding külliye (mosque complex) including its historic cemetery and the tombs of Suleiman the Magnificent and his wife Hürrem Sultan.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Beyoğlu district and the famous İstiklal Avenue — a pedestrian boulevard lined with historic buildings, shops, and restaurants. Ride the historic Tünel funicular.

meals.breakfast: Traditional Turkish breakfast at a neighborhood kahvaltı place near the hotel.
meals.lunch: Lunch in the Süleymaniye area — try a traditional lokanta for home-style Turkish cooking (ev yemekleri).
meals.dinner: Dinner on or near İstiklal Avenue — explore the side streets (meyhanes in Çiçek Pasajı passage) for affordable and flavorful options.

day_by_day.notes: The Basilica Cistern is particularly atmospheric — a must-see. Book tickets in advance online. Modest dress required at Süleymaniye Mosque.

day_by_day.morning: Take a Bosphorus Strait cruise — either a public ferry (economical and authentic) or a private guided boat tour. See the Dolmabahçe Palace, Rumeli Fortress, Bosphorus Bridge, and beautiful waterfront yalıs (wooden mansions) from the water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at Rumeli Hisarı (Rumeli Fortress) — a well-preserved 15th-century Ottoman fortress with great views. Explore the historic Bebek neighborhood — one of Istanbul's most elegant waterfront villages.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the city center. Visit the Beşiktaş fish market and surrounding streets for a lively local atmosphere. Enjoy a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — a full spread to fuel a long day on the water.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a casual fish restaurant in Bebek or Sarıyer — fresh grilled sea bass (levrek) or sea bream (çipura) with salad.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Beşiktaş — mid-range Turkish restaurant serving classic dishes like İskender kebab or hünkar beğendi (sultan's delight eggplant with lamb).

day_by_day.notes: Public Bosphorus ferries (IDO/Şehir Hatları) are very affordable and run regularly. For a more guided experience, book a private tour. Bring sunscreen and a light jacket for the boat.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Chora Church (Kariye Camii/Museum) in the Edirnekapı district — home to some of the finest Byzantine mosaics and frescoes in the world, dating from the 14th century.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Fener and Balat neighborhoods — two of Istanbul's oldest and most colorful districts. Stroll past rainbow-painted houses, Greek Orthodox churches, synagogues, and Ottoman-era architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Pierre Loti Hill (Eyüp) for sweeping views of the Golden Horn. Take the cable car up. Then explore the Eyüp Sultan Mosque and surrounding cemetery — a deeply spiritual and historically significant site.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café in Balat — the neighborhood is known for charming, photogenic cafés.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Balat restaurant — try traditional dishes in a historic setting. The area has excellent affordable eateries.
meals.dinner: Return to the hotel area or a nearby neighborhood — try a mid-range Turkish restaurant for meze and grilled meats.

day_by_day.notes: Balat and Fener are best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes on the hilly cobblestone streets. This area is less touristy and very authentic. Check opening hours for Chora Church in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Dolmabahçe Palace (Dolmabahçe Sarayı) — a stunning 19th-century Ottoman palace on the Bosphorus shore, blending European Baroque and Ottoman styles. See the 4.5-ton crystal chandelier — the largest in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Beşiktaş waterfront and Çırağan Palace (now a luxury hotel — you can walk the grounds). Visit the nearby Yıldız Park — a forested hilltop park with pavilions and great views, once the private grounds of Sultan Abdülhamid II.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Nişantaşı district — Istanbul's upscale shopping and dining neighborhood. Window shop along Abdi İpekçi Street and enjoy dinner at one of the area's excellent restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Café lunch near Dolmabahçe — light sandwiches, salads, or a traditional pide.
meals.dinner: Dinner in Nişantaşı — mid-range modern Turkish cuisine restaurant, perhaps featuring contemporary interpretations of Ottoman recipes.

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires a guided tour (included in ticket price). Tours run at set times — book ahead. The palace is closed on Mondays and Thursdays.

day_by_day.morning: Relax and experience a traditional Turkish hammam (bath) — try the historic Çemberlitaş Hamamı or Süleymaniye Hamamı. Enjoy a full kese (exfoliation scrub) and köpük (foam massage) for an authentic cultural wellness experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Istanbul Museum of Turkish and Islamic Arts (Türk ve İslam Eserleri Müzesi) in Sultanahmet — housing an extraordinary collection of calligraphy, carpets, ceramics, and manuscripts. Then revisit Sultanahmet Square for any sites you may have missed.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a traditional whirling dervish (Sema) ceremony — a UNESCO-recognized spiritual performance of the Mevlevi Order. Several venues in Istanbul offer evening performances.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near Sultanahmet — fresh salads, çorba (soup), and bread at a lokanta.
meals.dinner: Pre-show dinner near the Sema venue — a mid-range Ottoman-style restaurant with traditional dishes.

day_by_day.notes: Book the hammam and Sema ceremony in advance. The hammam experience typically lasts 1.5–2 hours. The Sema ceremony is a respectful cultural/spiritual event — observe quietly and dress modestly.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Princes' Islands (Adalar) — take a ferry from Kabataş to Büyükada, the largest of the nine islands. Enjoy the car-free environment, Victorian-era mansions, pine forests, and stunning sea views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Büyükada by horse-drawn carriage (fayton) or bicycle — visit the hilltop Aya Yorgi (St. George) Monastery for panoramic views. Relax on the island's beaches or swim in the clear Marmara Sea.
day_by_day.evening: Return ferry to Istanbul in the evening. Enjoy a relaxed dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast before departure — simit and tea, or hotel breakfast.
meals.lunch: Lunch on Büyükada — fresh seafood at a waterfront restaurant on the island (mid-range, expect slightly higher prices due to island location).
meals.dinner: Casual dinner near the hotel or beachfront area — grilled fish or a simple Turkish meal.

day_by_day.notes: Ferries to Büyükada take about 1.5–2 hours from Kabataş. Check the ferry schedule and book return tickets in advance, especially on weekends when islands are popular with locals. Bring swimwear and sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Pera Museum (Pera Müzesi) in Beyoğlu — housing the famous Tortoise Trainer painting by Osman Hamdi Bey, plus Anatolian weights and measures, and rotating contemporary exhibitions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Taksim Square area and the CRR (Cemal Reşit Rey) Concert Hall gardens. Walk through the charming Cihangir neighborhood — beloved by artists and expats, with independent bookshops, antique stores, and cozy cafés overlooking the Bosphorus.
day_by_day.evening: Spend your final full evening revisiting your favorite spots or exploring any neighborhoods you haven't yet seen. Consider a rooftop bar in Beyoğlu for sunset cocktails with panoramic city views.

meals.breakfast: Special farewell Turkish breakfast at a well-regarded kahvaltı spot — try Van Kahvaltı Evi style breakfast with 20+ items.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Cihangir — a neighborhood café or bistro with modern Turkish fusion dishes.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a memorable mid-range restaurant — try a classic Ottoman-inspired menu with dishes like lamb tandir, stuffed eggplant (karnıyarık), and künefe (cheese pastry dessert) to end your Istanbul culinary journey.

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to pick up any last souvenirs — Turkish ceramics, evil eye (nazar boncuğu) charms, tea sets, or quality Turkish delight. The Cihangir antique shops are excellent for unique finds.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely last breakfast at the hotel. Take a final walk along the beachfront or nearby area to soak in last views of Istanbul. Pack and prepare for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time, visit any last-minute attractions nearby or spend time at a local çay bahçesi (tea garden) with a book. Transfer to Istanbul Airport for your departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul. Reflect on 13 incredible days of history, culture, and food in one of the world's most extraordinary cities.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — enjoy it leisurely on your last morning.
meals.lunch: Light lunch near the hotel or at the airport — a final döner wrap or Turkish pastry for the road.
meals.dinner: Airport dining or in-flight meal.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for Istanbul Airport check-in and security. Keep your luggage manageable if you've purchased souvenirs. Consider keeping some Turkish Lira for airport tips and last-minute purchases. Safe travels!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Istanbul Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Istanbul Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged from the airport to Aegean Bliss Resort in the Beachfront district, with a personal concierge greeting you at arrivals holding a name placard. Enjoy chilled welcome drinks and a scenic drive along the Bosphorus coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort and settle into your suite. Take a leisurely stroll along the beachfront promenade to orient yourself with the surroundings. Enjoy a welcome amenity in your room — typically champagne and seasonal fruits arranged by the resort. Spend the remaining afternoon relaxing on the private terrace or at the infinity pool overlooking the sea.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle introduction to Istanbul's culinary scene with a sunset cocktail at the resort's rooftop bar, followed by a private welcome dinner at the resort's signature fine-dining restaurant featuring modern Ottoman cuisine with panoramic Bosphorus views.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — arrival day
meals.lunch: Light mezze and fresh seafood at the resort's beachside restaurant upon check-in
meals.dinner: Signature Ottoman tasting menu at the resort's fine-dining restaurant — expect dishes like slow-cooked lamb tandir, stuffed sea bass with wild herbs, and baklava soufflé paired with Turkish wines

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange a private airport transfer through the resort concierge. Request early check-in if possible given the 13:00 arrival. Keep the first evening light to recover from travel. Ensure your passport is ready for hotel registration upon arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Topkapi Palace — the legendary seat of the Ottoman Empire. Explore the Imperial Treasury, the Harem quarters, and the sacred relics pavilion with an expert historian guide who provides exclusive access and context beyond standard tours. Arrive early to beat the crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through the adjacent Hagia Sophia Grand Mosque, one of the world's greatest architectural achievements — a private guide will explain its Byzantine origins, Ottoman transformation, and modern significance. Afterward, explore the Basilica Cistern, the atmospheric underground Byzantine water reservoir, recently renovated with dramatic lighting installations.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Sultanahmet followed by a private evening Bosphorus cruise on a luxury yacht, sailing past illuminated palaces, mosques, and the iconic bridges connecting Europe and Asia.

meals.breakfast: Lavish Turkish breakfast spread at the resort — simit, fresh cheeses, olives, eggs cooked to order, clotted cream with honey, seasonal jams, and Turkish tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Matbah Restaurant near Topkapi — a refined Ottoman palace cuisine restaurant serving historical recipes from the palace kitchens, such as chicken with walnut sauce and stuffed quince
meals.dinner: Pre-cruise mezze dinner at Balıkçı Sabahattin, one of Istanbul's most celebrated traditional seafood restaurants in Sultanahmet, followed by the private yacht experience with onboard champagne service

day_by_day.notes: Book Topkapi Palace tickets and Harem access well in advance — private guided entry recommended. The Basilica Cistern is a short walk from Hagia Sophia. Wear modest clothing for the mosque visit — scarves and shoe covers are available at the entrance. Confirm the yacht cruise booking with the concierge the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private tour of the Grand Bazaar with a cultural historian and a personal shopper — explore over 4,000 shops across 61 covered streets. Focus on authentic artisan workshops producing handmade ceramics, hand-woven carpets, gold jewelry, and antique Ottoman items. Skip the tourist traps with expert guidance.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Spice Bazaar (Egyptian Bazaar) for an immersive sensory experience — sample exotic spices, Turkish delight, dried fruits, and local delicacies. Continue to the nearby Rüstem Pasha Mosque, a hidden gem adorned with the finest Iznik tiles in Istanbul. End with a private calligraphy or Ebru (marbling art) workshop in a traditional atelier.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a private Whirling Dervishes (Sema) ceremony — a UNESCO-recognized spiritual ritual of the Mevlevi order — at an intimate historical venue, followed by dinner in Karaköy.

meals.breakfast: Turkish breakfast at the resort with a focus on local specialties — menemen (scrambled eggs with tomatoes and peppers), börek (savory pastry), and fresh-squeezed pomegranate juice
meals.lunch: Lunch at Pandeli Restaurant inside the Spice Bazaar — a historic Istanbul institution operating since 1901, serving classic Turkish dishes like stuffed mussels, lamb stew, and milk pudding
meals.dinner: Dinner at Karaköy Lokantası — a beloved upscale lokanta (traditional Turkish eatery) known for its market-fresh ingredients, seasonal menus, and elegant yet relaxed atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The Grand Bazaar is closed on Sundays — check the day of the week. Bring cash (Turkish Lira) for bazaar purchases even if cards are accepted; better prices are negotiated in cash. The private art workshop should be booked through the concierge in advance. Dress comfortably for extensive walking.

day_by_day.morning: Private full-day Bosphorus and Asian Side experience begins with a luxury ferry crossing to Kadıköy on the Asian side of Istanbul. Explore the vibrant Kadıköy Market — a food lover's paradise with stalls selling fresh produce, artisan cheeses, pickles, and street food. Join a private food tour with a local culinary guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Moda neighborhood — Istanbul's charming bohemian enclave on the Asian shore — for a leisurely walk along the seafront. Explore independent bookshops, vintage boutiques, and local cafés. Continue to Üsküdar to visit the Maiden's Tower (Kız Kulesi), the iconic islet tower in the middle of the Bosphorus, recently restored and reopened as a luxury café and restaurant.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the European side via private water taxi. Enjoy sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar in Beyoğlu before dinner in the upscale Nişantaşı district.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Progressive food tasting lunch during the Kadıköy Market tour — sample kokoreç, midye dolma (stuffed mussels), fresh fish sandwiches, simit with cheese, and Turkish pastries at various artisan stalls
meals.dinner: Dinner at Neolokal in Beyoğlu — one of Istanbul's most acclaimed fine-dining restaurants led by Chef Maksut Aşkar, celebrating Anatolian ingredients through a modern tasting menu with wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: The Kadıköy food tour is best experienced in the morning when produce is freshest. Wear comfortable walking shoes. The Maiden's Tower requires advance reservations for dining — visit for coffee and views if dinner reservations aren't available. Keep some Turkish Lira for market purchases and tips.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Dolmabahçe Palace — the magnificent 19th-century Ottoman palace on the European shores of the Bosphorus, serving as the administrative center of the late Ottoman Empire. Marvel at the world's largest Bohemian crystal chandelier (gifted by Queen Victoria), the ornate ceremonial halls, and the Harem quarters with exclusive access.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Beşiktaş neighborhood and the nearby Çırağan Palace (now a Kempinski hotel) — walk the grounds and enjoy afternoon tea in their legendary setting. Visit the Istanbul Naval Museum to discover the Ottoman Empire's seafaring history through extraordinary imperial caiques (royal rowing boats) and maritime artifacts.
day_by_day.evening: Private Turkish hammam (bath) experience at one of Istanbul's most historic and luxurious bathhouses — a traditional cleansing ritual including a full-body scrub (kese), foam massage, and relaxation in the marble steam room.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Tuğra Restaurant inside the Çırağan Palace Kempinski — an iconic Ottoman fine-dining experience with palace views of the Bosphorus, serving dishes like lamb with eggplant purée and Ottoman-style pilafs
meals.dinner: Light dinner after the hammam at Zuma Istanbul in Beşiktaş — the globally renowned Japanese-inspired izakaya with stunning Bosphorus views, offering premium sushi, robata-grilled meats, and innovative cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Dolmabahçe Palace requires separate tickets for the Selamlık (ceremonial halls) and Harem — purchase the combined ticket. Photography is restricted inside. For the hammam, book the VIP private suite to avoid sharing the space with other guests. Kılıç Ali Paşa Hamamı or Çemberlitaş Hamamı are top luxury options.

day_by_day.morning: Private tour of the Istanbul Archaeology Museums — a world-class complex housing one of the finest collections of ancient artifacts in the world, including the stunning Alexander Sarcophagus, ancient Mesopotamian tablets, and the Treaty of Kadesh (the world's oldest known peace treaty). Guided by a specialist archaeologist.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Sultanahmet district on foot — visit the Hippodrome of Constantinople (ancient chariot racing arena), the German Fountain, the Serpentine Column, and the Blue Mosque (Sultan Ahmed Mosque) with its 20,000 hand-painted Iznik tiles. Enjoy a leisurely walk through the atmospheric streets of the old city.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive rooftop dining experience with a view of the illuminated Blue Mosque and Hagia Sophia — one of Istanbul's most iconic panoramas.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Seasons Restaurant at the Four Seasons Hotel Sultanahmet — an elegant courtyard restaurant set in a converted Ottoman prison, offering Mediterranean and Turkish cuisine in a serene garden setting
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sarnıç Restaurant — a romantic fine-dining restaurant set inside a 1,500-year-old Byzantine cistern near Hagia Sophia, serving contemporary Turkish cuisine with an extraordinary atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The Archaeology Museums complex includes three separate buildings — allocate at least 2.5 hours. The Blue Mosque is closed to tourists during prayer times (approximately 5 times daily) — plan your visit accordingly. Modest dress required for the mosque. Sarnıç Restaurant requires advance reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Princes' Islands (Adalar) — a group of nine car-free islands in the Sea of Marmara, a beloved escape from the city. Take a private luxury boat to Büyükada (the largest island) and explore by horse-drawn carriage or bicycle through pine forests, Victorian-era mansions, and secluded beaches.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Büyükada's charming village center — visit the historic Greek Orthodox Monastery of St. George perched on the island's highest hill, browse the artisan shops along the main promenade, and relax at a waterfront café. Swim in the clear Marmara Sea if weather permits.
day_by_day.evening: Return by private boat to Istanbul at sunset — the skyline of minarets and domes glowing in the golden light is a spectacular sight. Enjoy a quiet evening at the resort.

meals.breakfast: Picnic breakfast prepared by the resort and enjoyed on the private boat during the crossing
meals.lunch: Lunch at Miltos Restaurant on Büyükada — the island's most celebrated seafood restaurant, serving fresh catch of the day, grilled octopus, and local fish with Aegean mezze
meals.dinner: Dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant — a relaxed evening enjoying Ottoman-inspired cuisine after a full day of exploration

day_by_day.notes: The Princes' Islands are best visited on weekdays to avoid weekend crowds. Arrange the private boat charter through the resort concierge. The horse-drawn carriage ride around the island takes approximately 1.5 hours. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and swimwear. The monastery hike is moderately challenging — wear appropriate footwear.

day_by_day.morning: Immersive private cooking class with a renowned Istanbul chef — learn to prepare classic Turkish dishes from scratch, including homemade börek, slow-cooked lamb güveç (clay pot stew), stuffed grape leaves (dolma), and traditional baklava. Visit a local market beforehand to select fresh ingredients.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the vibrant Galata neighborhood — climb the 14th-century Galata Tower for panoramic 360-degree views of Istanbul spanning both continents. Wander through the antique dealers and art galleries of the surrounding streets. Cross the iconic Galata Bridge and observe local fishermen casting their lines.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the legendary İstiklal Avenue (Independence Avenue) — Istanbul's most famous pedestrian boulevard lined with historic architecture, international brands, independent boutiques, and cultural institutions. Attend a classical Turkish music concert or a contemporary art exhibition in one of the nearby venues.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Enjoy the dishes prepared during the cooking class as a sit-down lunch with the chef and fellow participants, paired with local wines and ayran
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mikla Restaurant — one of Istanbul's most iconic fine-dining destinations atop the Marmara Pera hotel, offering New Nordic-meets-Anatolian cuisine by Chef Mehmet Gürs with breathtaking city views

day_by_day.notes: The cooking class should be booked well in advance through a reputable culinary school such as Istanbul Culinary Institute or a private chef arrangement via the concierge. The Galata Tower can have long queues — purchase tickets online in advance. Mikla requires reservations weeks ahead, especially for window tables.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Topkapi Palace Museum's lesser-known sections — the Imperial Stables, the Outer Treasury, and the Porcelain Collection featuring thousands of Chinese and Japanese pieces collected by Ottoman sultans. Followed by a visit to the nearby Gülhane Park, the oldest public park in Istanbul, once the outer garden of the palace.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Fener and Balat neighborhoods — two of Istanbul's oldest and most atmospheric districts on the Golden Horn, home to colorful Ottoman-era houses, historic Greek and Jewish communities, Byzantine churches, and independent art galleries. A private guide will bring the layered history of these communities to life.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a rooftop bar overlooking the Golden Horn, followed by a private dinner cruise along the Golden Horn waterway.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at a traditional lokanta in Balat — try Forno Balat for artisan sourdough and local specialties, or a neighborhood meyhane (tavern) for homestyle Turkish cooking with seasonal dishes and rakı
meals.dinner: Private dinner on a luxury Golden Horn cruise boat — a curated menu of Turkish mezze, grilled fish, and desserts served as the boat glides past Byzantine walls, historic shipyards, and illuminated bridges

day_by_day.notes: Fener and Balat are best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes as the streets are cobblestoned and hilly. The neighborhood is undergoing gentrification but retains authentic character. Photography opportunities are exceptional — bring a good camera. Arrange the Golden Horn dinner cruise through the resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private day trip to Edirne — the former Ottoman capital located approximately 2.5 hours from Istanbul by private car. Visit the Selimiye Mosque, considered the architectural masterpiece of the great Ottoman architect Mimar Sinan, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. Explore the Old Mosque and the Beyazit II Mosque complex.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Edirne — visit the historic Kırkpınar Oil Wrestling Arena (home to the world's oldest sporting event), the Ali Pasha Covered Bazaar, and the beautifully restored Edirne Palace ruins. Sample Edirne's famous local specialties including liver (ciğer) and cheese.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Istanbul by private car in the late afternoon. Enjoy a relaxing evening at the resort — spa treatment, pool, or a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the resort before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch in Edirne at a local restaurant specializing in Edirne cuisine — Edirne tava ciğeri (fried liver), white cheese from Edirne, and local pastries
meals.dinner: Light dinner at the resort's restaurant or room service after the long day trip

day_by_day.notes: Depart by 08:00 to maximize time in Edirne. Private car hire is strongly recommended over public transport for comfort and flexibility. Edirne is a half-day to full-day destination — this itinerary covers the highlights. Carry cash as some establishments in Edirne may not accept cards. The Selimiye Mosque is free to enter.

day_by_day.morning: Private visit to the Sakıp Sabancı Museum in Emirgan — one of Turkey's finest private art museums, set in a stunning Bosphorus-side villa. The collection includes Ottoman calligraphy, paintings, and rotating world-class international exhibitions. The museum gardens offer spectacular Bosphorus views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the upscale Nişantaşı district — Istanbul's answer to Paris's 7th arrondissement, home to flagship luxury boutiques, concept stores, art galleries, and beautifully preserved early 20th-century architecture. Enjoy a private personal shopping session with a local style consultant if desired.
day_by_day.evening: Attend a performance at the Istanbul Opera or a concert at the Cemal Reşit Rey Concert Hall — check the program for May 2027. Follow with a late dinner in the Beşiktaş or Ortaköy neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the resort
meals.lunch: Lunch at Müzedechanga at the Sakıp Sabancı Museum — an acclaimed restaurant with terraced Bosphorus views, serving contemporary Mediterranean-Turkish cuisine using seasonal local ingredients
meals.dinner: Dinner at Banyan Restaurant in Ortaköy — a sophisticated Pan-Asian restaurant with a stunning terrace overlooking the Bosphorus and the illuminated Ortaköy Mosque, perfect for a special evening

day_by_day.notes: Check the Sakıp Sabancı Museum's current exhibitions before visiting — temporary shows often feature internationally significant works. Nişantaşı shopping is best on weekday afternoons. Book opera or concert tickets well in advance through the Istanbul State Opera and Ballet website. Ortaköy is lively in the evenings — arrive by reservation.

day_by_day.morning: Private helicopter tour of Istanbul — experience the city from above in a luxury helicopter, soaring over the Bosphorus, the historic peninsula, the Golden Horn, the Princes' Islands, and both the European and Asian shores. A truly once-in-a-lifetime perspective on one of the world's most visually stunning cities.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Pera Museum in Beyoğlu — an exceptional private museum housing the famous Orientalist paintings collection, Anatolian weights and measures, and Kütahya tiles. The museum's crown jewel is Giovanni Battista Tiepolo's 'The Torture of Two Saints' and Osman Hamdi Bey's iconic 'The Tortoise Trainer.' Browse the surrounding Pera/Tepebaşı neighborhood's historic architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell luxury dinner at one of Istanbul's most exclusive and celebrated restaurants — a grand finale to the culinary journey.

meals.breakfast: Special champagne breakfast at the resort — a celebratory spread to mark the penultimate day
meals.lunch: Lunch at Pera Museum Café — light bites and Turkish coffee in the museum's elegant café setting
meals.dinner: Grand farewell dinner at Sunset Grill & Bar in Ulus — perched on a hillside with panoramic Bosphorus views, offering a sophisticated menu of Turkish and international cuisine, an extensive wine cellar, and impeccable service

day_by_day.notes: The helicopter tour must be booked well in advance through a licensed operator — the resort concierge can arrange this. Flights typically last 20–45 minutes depending on the package. Weather conditions affect helicopter tours — have a backup plan. The Pera Museum is closed on Mondays. Sunset Grill & Bar requires advance reservations, especially for terrace seating.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Istanbul — leisurely breakfast at the resort followed by a last stroll along the beachfront promenade. Visit any remaining sites or boutiques on your personal wish list. Consider a final Turkish coffee and baklava at a traditional café as a farewell ritual.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Aegean Bliss Resort. Private luxury transfer to Istanbul Airport for departure. The concierge will arrange luggage handling, checkout formalities, and ensure a seamless transfer experience.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Istanbul — carry with you the memories of 13 extraordinary days exploring one of the world's most magnificent cities.

meals.breakfast: Final lavish Turkish breakfast at the resort — savor every last bite of fresh simit, clotted cream, honey, and çay (tea)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport's premium lounge or a quick stop at a quality café near the hotel before transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Arrange checkout the evening before to streamline the morning. Allow at least 3 hours before your flight for international departures from Istanbul Airport. The resort concierge can assist with last-minute gift wrapping, shipping of purchased items, and currency exchange. Keep valuables and travel documents in your carry-on bag.
